newsitem.title: USA: Trade sees light USDA weekly export sales numbers.
newsitem.headline: Trade sees light USDA weekly export sales numbers.

text.p: Grain and soy traders at the Chicago Board of Trade expect light to moderate numbers for grains and soybean exports in the U.S. Agriculture Department's 0730 CST/1330 GMT release Thursday of weekly sales.
"Two to three hundred (thousand tonnes) wheat and closer to two hundred would be safer," a trader said.

Trades estimates for U.S. net export sales for wheat during the week ended December 5 ranged from 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes. The net export tally the previous week was 82,900 tonnes, compiled during the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday trading week.
Corn and soybean sales numbers also were seen light to modest.
"Japan, and the rest of Asia for that matter, are pretty well covered for now," another trader said.
The market expected corn net export sales the week ended December 5 of 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes, above the "surprisingly low" 242,800 tonnes reported the previous week.

Soybean net exports were estimated from 450,000 to 550,000 tonnes, about the same as the 534,400 tonnes the previous week. Soyoil estimates ranged from 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes and soymeal exports were pegged at 50,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
For the week ended November 28, export sales of soyoil were at 15,400 tonnes and soymeal ran at a deficit during the week of 11,200 tonnes.
